sources.citation: Rodríguez González, María Ángeles. 1992. Lenguaje de signos. Madrid: Confederación Nacional de Sordos de España / Fundación ONCE. (Glottolog ref 551794; archive.org item rodriguez_-_lenguaje_de_signos, a re-typeset digital edition with the print page numbers embedded)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Ch. III 'Articulación del signo gestual' (pp. 103-141) analyses signs into six formative parameters (queirema, toponema, kinema, kineprosema, queirotropema, prosoponema); no stress/accent/intensity parameter and 'acento' never occurs in a linguistic sense. Closest passages are phrase-level: p. 17 (rhythm of manual movement is an expressive subcomponent), p. 56 ('un ritmo de articulación más lento del signo que interesa poner de relieve y que suele situarse en posición final, a veces, incluso, con movimiento repetido y mediante el juego de pausas'), pp. 140-141 (slower finger flexion/extension…

sources.citation: Quer, Josep (ed.) [PDF title page: "Edited by Kelepir Meltem"]. 2020. Topics in the Grammar of Spanish Sign Language (LSE). SIGN-HUB Sign Language Grammar Series, 1st ed. Online: https://thesignhub.eu/grammar/lse (Glottolog ref 588526 'Meltem 2020')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The 30-page PDF (Jan 2020) is the full Blueprint table of contents plus a few written Lexicon sections (pronouns, by Raquel Veiga Busto). Part 2 Phonology, Chapter 2 'Prosody' lists 2.1.1 Syllable, 2.1.2 Foot, 2.2.1 Prosodic word etc., but the online sections (thesignhub.eu/grammar/lse?tag=100/101/103/105) all return 'This part has no content'. No text on stress exists in this grammar.

sources.citation: Herrero Blanco, Ángel & Juan José Alfaro Abellán. 1999. Fonología y escritura de la lengua de signos española. ELUA: Estudios de Lingüística, Universidad de Alicante 13: 89-116. DOI 10.14198/ELUA1999.13.04; handle 10045/6302
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Proposes the LSE 's-sílaba' L C Q O (M F) with handshape Q as nucleus; 'sílaba breve' vs 'sílaba larga' is defined by presence of movement M/F, not by prominence (p. 96); mentions non-distinctive gradable 'intensidad' of a sign and 'prosodia facial' (pp. 102-103). Nothing on stress or accent placement.
